leads_to.evidence: APA reports that close to half of psychology bachelor's holders go on to earn a graduate degree, often outside psychology. Becoming a psychologist takes a doctorate, and counseling roles require a master's.

nearby_pair.evidence: Walden's BS in Psychology is an online program for adult learners. Applicants must be 21 or older, have college credits, or be military, and it accepts up to 135 transfer credits. A new high-school graduate cannot usually choose between it and the Minneapolis campus program.

school_matters.evidence: Psychology has no license at the bachelor's level, so pay does not set a floor at entry. Graduates of every kind of school compete for the same broad entry jobs, and APA data show many graduates work outside psychology. The gap between the bands is modest.

who_is_counted.evidence: Southern New Hampshire University awards by far the most general psychology degrees and mostly enrolls adult and online students. The next largest are big public universities such as Central Florida and Florida International, which mostly enroll traditional undergraduates.

programs.evidence: Stanford admits a tiny share of applicants, and its graduates are recruited by top employers in tech, consulting and finance whatever their major.
Santa Clara sits in the San Jose metro area, where wages in nearly every occupation run far above the national level, so local pay lifts its graduates' earnings.
Colgate is a highly selective liberal arts college whose graduates are recruited heavily into finance, consulting and other high-paying first jobs.
Wages in Puerto Rico are far below mainland levels across occupations, and that alone explains the low first-year pay at Rio Piedras.
The Arecibo campus reports exactly the same earnings, debt and cohort as the Ponce campus, so its figures appear to be pooled across the university's campuses. Low Puerto Rico wages also play a part.
